titulo: The goodbye that gets you invited back
subtitulo: The last sentence of the course is the same shape as the first one — said to someone before you need anything from them
cena: It is the last morning, the same four faces are where they have been all week, and you have about a minute with each of them.
frasePiso: Name the person, name the thing they did, say you are coming back. Three clauses, and the door stays open.

steps.pt: This course opened with a greeting given before you needed anything. It closes with one given when you no longer need anything.
The formula has three parts: the person, the specific thing, and the return. Miss the middle one and it is just politeness.

steps.promptPt: Say goodbye to the person at the bar who served you every morning. Speak now.
steps.es: Grazie di tutto, davvero. Il caffè migliore della città.
steps.pinyin: GRA-tsee-eh dee TOOT-to, dav-VE-ro. eel kaf-FEH mee-LYO-re DEL-la cheet-TA
steps.pt: Thanks for everything, really. The best coffee in the city.
steps.tts: Grazie di tutto, davvero. Il caffè migliore della città.

steps.acao: Answer the invitation rather than just smiling at it. That is the whole part.
steps.es: Ma quando torni? Che ti aspetto, eh!
steps.pt: So when are you coming back? I'll be expecting you!
steps.tts: Ma quando torni? Che ti aspetto, eh!

steps.promptPt: Answer with something specific, not with maybe. Speak now.
steps.es: L'anno prossimo, in primavera. Te lo prometto.
steps.pinyin: LAN-no PROS-see-mo, een pree-ma-VE-ra. teh lo pro-MET-to
steps.pt: Next year, in spring. I promise you.
steps.tts: L'anno prossimo, in primavera. Te lo prometto.

steps.pt: A vague maybe closes the door politely. A season and a promise keeps it open, and people do remember.

steps.promptPt: Say goodbye to the family who had you to lunch. Speak now.
steps.es: Non dimenticheremo quel pranzo. Siete stati gentilissimi.
steps.pinyin: non dee-men-tee-ke-RE-mo kwel PRAN-tso. see-EH-te STA-tee jen-tee-LEES-see-mee
steps.pt: We won't forget that lunch. You were extremely kind.
steps.tts: Non dimenticheremo quel pranzo. Siete stati gentilissimi.

steps.pt: Then the pocket card. Six sentences that carried the whole trip, and they are all from the first module.

steps.acao: Every one of these you can now produce without thinking. That is what the course was.
steps.es: Buongiorno. Posso? Dov'è? C'è? Quanto costa? Grazie mille.
steps.pt: Good morning. May I? Where is? Is there? How much? Thank you very much.
steps.tts: Buongiorno. Posso? Dov'è? C'è? Quanto costa? Grazie mille.

steps.promptPt: The one that rescues everything else. Speak now.
steps.es: Scusi, non ho capito. Me lo può ripetere?
steps.pinyin: SKOO-zee, non oh ka-PEE-to. meh lo pwoh ree-PE-te-re
steps.pt: Sorry, I didn't understand. Could you repeat it?
steps.tts: Scusi, non ho capito. Me lo può ripetere?

steps.pt: That sentence is the real product. Everything else is easier to look up; that one has to be automatic.

steps.promptPt: Close the trip the way Italians close things — not with goodbye but with next time. Speak now.

steps.acao: In bocca al lupo is good luck. The answer is crepi, or crepi il lupo.
steps.es: In bocca al lupo per il viaggio! Buon rientro.
steps.pt: Good luck for the journey! Safe trip home.
steps.tts: In bocca al lupo per il viaggio! Buon rientro.

steps.promptPt: Give the answer that only someone who has been paying attention knows. Speak now.
steps.es: Crepi il lupo! Grazie di cuore.
steps.pinyin: KRE-pee eel LOO-po! GRA-tsee-eh dee KWO-re
steps.pt: May the wolf die! Thank you from the heart.
steps.tts: Crepi il lupo! Grazie di cuore.

steps.pt: That is the course. Six sentences, seven frames, and the one that rescues the rest. Buon viaggio — and alla prossima.

secoes.corpo: Buongiorno. Posso…? Dov'è…? C'è…? Quanto costa…? Grazie mille. Between them they open a conversation, ask permission, find a place, check that a thing exists, protect your money and close warmly. Everything else in the course hangs off these.

exemplos.es: Scusi, non ho capito. Me lo può ripetere?
exemplos.pt: Sorry, I didn't understand. Could you repeat it?

secoes.titulo: The repair sentence is the product
secoes.corpo: Non ho capito, me lo può ripetere is the one that has to be automatic, because it is what keeps every other sentence usable when the answer comes back faster than you expected.

Into the wolf's mouth, and may the wolf die. A superstitious good-luck exchange where saying grazie is considered bad form. Knowing the reply is a small marker that you were paying attention all week.

Italian closes with next time rather than with finality. Arrivederci itself means until we see each other again. That is not a coincidence — it is the same instinct that this whole module has been about.

permissao: You are allowed to promise to come back and mean it loosely. Naming a season rather than saying maybe is not a commitment anyone will hold you to — it is the form the goodbye takes here, and it is why the person behind the counter remembers you next year.
espelho: Anyone who has left a place they loved with a wave and thought afterwards about the sentence they did not say knows what this last part is for. It costs one minute per person, and it is the only part of a trip you can still improve on the way out.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Someone wishes you in bocca al lupo before a journey or an exam, and you start to say grazie.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Someone wished me luck, so thanks is the obvious reply.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: It is a superstitious formula with a fixed answer, and thanking someone for it is held to break the charm. The expected reply is crepi, or crepi il lupo.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer crepi il lupo. It takes two words and it is the sort of thing visitors almost never know.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The exchange completes the way it is meant to, and you get the small delighted reaction that comes from a foreigner producing exactly the right formula.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not with every good-luck wish — buona fortuna takes a normal grazie, and only the wolf formula carries the superstition.
